scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a configuration change on router8, router7 reports that its
OSPF adjacency with router8 dropped (neighbor went INIT/DOWN, then
gone) and some Campus 2 routes flapped. Campus-1-to-Campus-1
traffic still works and Campus 2 PCs reach their local SVI. Find
what broke the router7<->router8 adjacency.

injection.action: change OSPF area for the 172.25.1.0 network to a
injection.command:
vtysh -c "configure terminal" \
        -c "router ospf" \
        -c "no network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0" \
        -c "network 172.25.1.0/24 area 7" \
        -c "exit" -c "exit"
  vtysh -c "clear ip ospf process"

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router8 OSPF area configuration on the
  172.25.1.0/24 link
Mechanism: OSPF requires both ends of an adjacency to agree
  on the area ID. router7's eth5 is 172.25.1.1 in area 0;
  router8's eth4 was 172.25.1.2 in area 0 and was just changed
  to area 7. The hellos now carry mismatched area IDs, so the
  router7<->router8 adjacency drops (Full -> Init -> gone).
  router8 remains in OSPF via its OTHER area-0 links, so traffic
  reroutes and Campus 1 stays mostly reachable -- the observable,
  diagnosable fault is the dropped adjacency on the 172.25.1.0/24
  link, not a full Campus-2 outage.
Localization: router8
Root cause: OSPF area mismatch on the router7<->router8 link
  (router8 in area 7, router7 in area 0)
Fix: on router8 — `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "no network
  172.25.1.0/24 area 7" -c "network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0"`
scenario.fix_spec:
on router8 — `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "no network
  172.25.1.0/24 area 7" -c "network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0"`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: OSPF area assignment / area mismatch

agent.diagnosis_text:
The OSPF adjacency between router7 and router8 over the 172.25.1.0/24 segment
(link_lan_172_25_1; router7.eth5 ↔ router8.eth4) is broken by an OSPF area
mismatch introduced via a configuration change on router8.

Affected component: OSPF network-statement on router8, specifically the area
assignment for the 172.25.1.0/24 prefix.

Mechanism: OSPF embeds the Area ID in every Hello packet. A router that receives
a Hello with a mismatched Area ID silently discards it; the neighbor state never
advances past INIT and eventually times out to DOWN/gone. Both sides have been
independently elected DR on the segment (each sees 0 neighbors), which is the
classic symptom of an area-ID mismatch on a broadcast segment.

Localization:
  • router7 eth5 (172.25.1.1/24) — Area 0.0.0.0 (correct, backbone)
  • router8 eth4 (172.25.1.2/24) — Area 0.0.0.7 (wrong; this is a non-backbone
    stub area that has no other members, explaining the "0 fully adjacent
    neighbors" in area 0.0.0.7 on router8's OSPF process)

The 172.29.10.0/24 link (router8 ↔ router17) is correctly placed in Area 0, so
router8's other adjacency is unaffected.

Root cause: After the configuration change on router8, the network statement for
172.25.1.0/24 was (re)configured as `network 172.25.1.0/24 area 7` instead of
`network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0`, placing router8's side of the r7–r8 link in a
non-backbone area while router7 continues to advertise the same subnet into Area 0.

Corrective fix: On router8, enter the OSPF process and correct the area:
  conf t → router ospf →
    no network 172.25.1.0/24 area 7
    network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0
  write memory
This will immediately re-match router7's area 0 Hello, the adjacency will reform,
and the Campus-2 route flap will stabilize.

per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies router8 as the device with the misconfigured OSPF area.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: OSPF area assignment / area mismatch
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies an OSPF area assignment/network-statement mismatch on router8 for 172.25.1.0/24 (area 7 vs area 0).
The agent explicitly names the affected link as the 172.25.1.0/24 segment between router7.eth5 and router8.eth4 (router7<->router8), matching the required identification.
The agent clearly explains how OSPF includes Area ID in Hellos, how mismatched IDs prevent adjacency formation (stuck in INIT and timing out), and links this to DR elections and observed symptoms.
The agent prescribes removing the wrong area statement on router8 and re-adding the network in area 0 (then saving), which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log contains the necessary outputs (neighbor lists, running-configs, and interface OSPF area assignments) showing router7 on area 0 and router8 advertising 172.25.1.0/24 in area 7, with the adjacency absent and interfaces up. The writeup's inference (area mismatch causing adjacency drop) follows directly and addresses alternatives.
